newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek PM-elect has mandate for new government.
newsitem.headline: Greek PM-elect has mandate for new government.

text.p: Greek prime minister-elect Costas Simitis said on Monday he had received a mandate from President Costis Stephanopoulos to form a four-year socialist government.
"The president has given me the order to form a new government. I shall present the government within the next few days," he told reporters outside the presidential residence.
Simitis said he wanted to wait to see the final results of Sunday's election so he could take into account the popularity of individual socialist deputies.
Under the mandate he has three days to form a government. It must then pass a confidence vote in the 300-seat parliament.
He won a solid victory over the opposition conservatives in the election, taking about 41.5 percent of the vote and 162 seats -- a clear absolute majority.
Simitis, 60, is expected to make major changes in the cabinet which he inherited in January when he took over as prime minister from late socialist party founder Andreas Papandreou.
